 Ben Kindel suffers "medical episode" on Penguins plane, team says
 By
 Madeline Bartos 
 Updated on: October 20, 2026 / 5:02 PM EDT 
 / CBS Pittsburgh
 Add CBS News on Google 
 Forward Ben Kindel  suffered a "medical episode" on the Pittsburgh Penguins' team plane shortly after taking off in Salt Lake City on Tuesday, the team said.
 Kindel — who the Penguins said is conscious, alert and in stable condition — was taken to the University of Utah Hospital for further evaluation. 
 In a statement posted to social media, the Penguins said that shortly after takeoff, the team plane returned to Salt Lake City International Airport because of a "medical episode" involving Kindel. The team's physician and medical staff were on board and "immediately attended to Ben," the Penguins said. 
 The team didn't provide any other details on Kindel's situation, but said, "The health and safety of our players, as well as the privacy for their families, are our top priority." 
 The Penguins said more details will be shared "when appropriate." 
 The 19-year-old Canadian was drafted 11th overall in 2025. So far this season, he's scored two goals and recorded two assists.
